author: CC
prose: Fingerprint what the proof exercises, not the directory it sits in. At seal time the tester already runs the proof in a subprocess. Have the proof report which component files it imported (the module table at exit) and hash only that set plus the proof file. Then an edit to one module expires only proofs that load it. The horizon wording already says 'the code it proves'. This is the finer form of the yellow residue on ticket 1b6516f92db3, and it is deterministic. The honest hole: a proof that reads a file with open() rather than importing it is not caught, so the record should say the fingerprint is the import closure. Measured 2026-09-05: one edit to transitions.py expired 30 tools/base proofs; 60 of 154 seals expired at that moment. Akien 2026-09-06: 'i agree about your optimizations all the way thru.'
